newsitem.title: CHILE: Four escape by helicopter from Chilean prison.
newsitem.headline: Four escape by helicopter from Chilean prison.

text.p: Four prisoners were whisked off the roof of a high-security Chilean prison in a daring escape on Monday, authorities said.

The convicts, including two left-wing guerrilla leaders, climbed a rope ladder dangling from the helicopter over the heavily fortified jail in Santiago, but a fifth man fell back onto the roof after being shot at by prison guards, witnesses said.
"A helicopter flew over for a while and then they threw down a ladder...there were shots and one man fell back down," said witness David Leon.
Two of the escaped men were leaders of the left-wing terrorist group Manuel Rodriguez Patriotic Front, said Interior Minister Carlos Figueroa.
"Two escaped prisoners are the most important people in the Patriotic Front, Palma Salamanca and Hernandez Norambuena, as well as two others..." said Figueroa.
Deputy Justice Jose Antonio Gomez later identified the other two men as Pablo Munoz and Patricio Ortiz, both of whom were members of the front.
The helicopter, which was rented, landed in a nearby park where its occupants got into a waiting car, police sources said.

Police said they later found the vehicle used in the escape with two M-16 rifles in a park in the south of the city. A second vehicle used by the group has not yet been found, they said, and police were searching for the men who escaped.

The Manuel Rodriguez Patriotic Front was involved in a spate of assassinations and kidnappings in Chile during Gen. Augusto Pinochet's military government and in the first years of democratic rule in the early 1990s.
